course.title: C — Complete Deep Learning Course
course.description: A genuinely C-specific, beginner-to-advanced course with concept-first notes, practical coding, dedicated tasks, testing and a complete capstone.
course.curriculumPolicy: Module and lesson counts are determined by the concepts required to learn this language properly; no fixed module/lesson template is imposed.
learningOutcomes: Understand C from fundamentals to advanced practical programming.

modules.title: C Foundations
modules.description: Compilation, main, variables, primitive types and standard I/O.

lessons.title: C Foundations
lessons.description: Compilation, main, variables, primitive types and standard I/O.
learningObjectives: Understand the mental model behind C Foundations.
Write correct C code using C Foundations.
Explain the program flow in your own words.
Handle at least one edge case.
Apply the concept in a practical task.

notes.text: Compilation, main, variables, primitive types and standard I/O.
In this lesson, the student should understand c foundations before trying to memorize syntax. Start with the mental model, then connect each rule to a small program and finally to the practical task.
C Foundations is important because it appears repeatedly when building real C programs. A student should be able to explain when to use it, what can go wrong, and how to test the result.

notes.caption: Create a teaching diagram showing the relationship between the main ideas in C Foundations.

items: Define the main idea behind C Foundations.
Understand the syntax or API involved.
Trace what happens step by step when the program runs.
Know the common failure cases.
Choose a clear and maintainable implementation.

notes.text: Read the example from top to bottom. Predict the result first. Then run it and compare your prediction with the actual result.

items: Identify the input or starting state.
Identify the important variables/data structures.
Follow each operation in order.
Observe the output or returned value.
Ask what would happen with invalid, empty, very large or unexpected input.
Copying syntax without understanding the data flow.
Ignoring invalid input or boundary cases.
Mixing responsibilities into one large function.
Failing to test the code after changing it.
Using a more complex technique when a simpler one is clearer.
Prefer readable names and small responsibilities.
Validate assumptions at boundaries.
Keep repeated logic reusable.
Test both expected and failure paths.
Use the official language documentation when behavior is uncertain.
I can explain C Foundations without reading the notes.
I can write a small example from memory.
I can identify at least one edge case.
I can explain one common mistake and how to avoid it.

practicals.title: Guided Practical — C Foundations
practicals.objective: Use C Foundations in a small but complete C exercise.
steps: Change the input and predict the result.
Test an invalid or boundary case.
practicals.expectedOutput: A working C program demonstrating C Foundations.

tasks.title: Dedicated Task — C Foundations
tasks.description: Build a command-line student welcome program.
requirements: The solution must demonstrate C Foundations.
Use clear naming and structure.
Validate relevant input.
Handle at least two edge cases.
Include a short README explaining the approach.
acceptanceCriteria: Student can explain the important code.

quiz.question: Which statement best describes C Foundations?
options: It is a core C programming concept covered in this lesson.
It is only a CSS feature.
quiz.answer: It is a core C programming concept covered in this lesson.
quiz.explanation: The lesson is specifically designed to make C Foundations understandable and usable in C.

quiz.question: What should you do after the first working implementation?
options: Test normal and edge cases, then refactor.
quiz.answer: Test normal and edge cases, then refactor.
quiz.explanation: Reliable programming requires validation beyond the happy path.

summary: C Foundations is understood through mental model, syntax, execution flow and practice.
The dedicated task applies the concept in a realistic context.
Students should be able to explain and implement the concept independently.
